History of Present Illness:
60-year-old woman. Fourteen hours of severe epigastric pain and vomiting. She has no alcohol exposure, known gallstones or recent procedures.

Physical Examination:
Epigastric tenderness; abdomen soft outside the upper central region. Temperature 37.7 C; heart rate 88/min; BP 122/78 mmHg; respiratory rate 22/min; SpO2 98% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 11.8 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.9 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 255 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 138 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 4.1 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 90 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 1390 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 33 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 30 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 95 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
Ultrasound abdomen: no gallstones or duct dilation; pancreas poorly visualized. No gallbladder wall thickening.
